options.text: An agreed limit on metrics and/or resource sizes that the team commits not to exceed
The number of developers on the team
A Lighthouse feature that speeds up the page

questions.explanation: A performance budget is an explicit, shared limit (on timings and/or bytes/requests) that turns speed into an enforceable target so regressions are caught deliberately.

questions.prompt: Match each budget concept to its meaning.

pairs.right: A limit on a timing like LCP or INP
A limit on bytes or request counts
A minimum tool score, e.g. Lighthouse ≥ 90
An unintended slowdown introduced by a change

questions.explanation: Metric budgets limit outcomes (timings), quantity budgets limit inputs (bytes/requests), score budgets set a minimum tool score, and a regression is an unintended slowdown.

questions.prompt: A budget only sticks if it's enforced automatically in ____, so a pull request that exceeds a limit fails the build (two letters).
questions.explanation: Enforcing budgets in CI (e.g. Lighthouse CI or a bundle-size check) fails a pull request that breaches a limit, catching regressions before they ship.

questions.prompt: Which are good performance-budget practices? Select all that apply.

options.text: Enforce the budget automatically in CI
Budget JavaScript separately, not just total bytes
Set an aspirational limit you routinely miss
Anchor limits to the Core Web Vitals "good" thresholds and current data

questions.explanation: Enforce in CI, budget JS on its own, and anchor to CWV and your real numbers. An always-missed limit trains everyone to ignore the failing check.

questions.prompt: Why should JavaScript get its own, tighter budget rather than just counting total bytes?

options.text: JavaScript files are always the largest files
Because JS must be downloaded, parsed, compiled, and executed on the main thread, making it the most expensive kind of byte
Because browsers refuse to cache JavaScript

questions.explanation: Byte for byte, JavaScript costs more than images or fonts because after download it is parsed, compiled, and executed on the main thread — so it warrants a dedicated limit.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of establishing a workable performance budget.

items.text: Set a realistic limit anchored to the CWV "good" thresholds
Enforce it in CI so breaches fail the build
Ratchet the limit tighter over time

questions.explanation: Start from where you are, set a holdable target, enforce it automatically, then tighten it as the team improves.
